reasoning: Set A follows the ground truth much more closely. It has a circular tank where fish survive as long as possible, a single learning predator, and a self-play rung with a proper opponent pool. It builds a ladder of tabular Q-learning, DQN and CNN-DQN for value learning, includes ablations, and compares REINFORCE with PPO. Its golden cases are precise known-answer cases, and the ones I checked by hand (TD update, GAE, clipped objective, reflection, catch distances) are correct. A's main weaknesses are leftover process text in the architecture ('adopted before M1 is built', 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change' when there are 71 cases), Exit wording that differs between the roadmap and the plan, and a very large M1. Set B has cleaner docs, a good check-world gate and a strong replay viewer design, but it drifts from the brief. Its tank is square, fish are hit and respawn with a lower-is-better score instead of surviving, it has 2 predators, and S3 is naive co-learning with no opponent pool. B's S1 split carves 'See, check and explain' (replay, reference check, write-up, plus an unmentioned DQN thicken) into M2. That leaves M1 with no replay viewer and no requirement that the snake actually learns. B's spines also fold in other components' modules (the train_loop spine builds runlog/writer.py; the DQN spine builds methods/factory.py). In both sets, the spine packets I sampled leave out types they need.

strengths: Faithful to all three stages: circular tank with survival score, one predator, rung-3 self-play from an opponent pool with cross-play and ratings
Precise golden cases with hand-checkable numbers (TC-12, TC-41–TC-43, TC-29, TC-52, TC-58)
Separates truncation from termination so learning targets bootstrap correctly; ablations teach exploration, replay memory and the target network
Comparison with a reference library implementation at each stage, with the settings mapped one to one
weaknesses: Process narration and stale counts left in the architecture
M1 is very large (31 tasks: three agents, corridor, reference, ablations, report, replay)
Exit criteria differ slightly between roadmap and plan
Spine packet T06 leaves out core.Transition and runs.create_run

strengths: Check-world gate (two-exit corridor) catches silent RL bugs before any batch runs
Clean, well-scoped contracts; the replay design (Trace re-simulation, side by side, sight overlay, video) is strong
Paired permutation test with Holm correction specified exactly; write-up support for the learner's own explanations
weaknesses: Tank is square, fish respawn and are scored on hits; 2 predators; no opponent-pool self-play in S3
M2 is a carved-off 'replay + reference + notes' milestone; M1 has no replay and doesn't require the snake to learn
Spines write other components' modules (runlog/writer.py, methods/factory.py)
Golden cases for Snake are weak property checks, and the observation layout is unspecified
